accepted_interpretation.source_support: Proposition 2 asks for an even, nonnegative C-infinity function f, normalized by f(0)=1 and compactly supported in [-B,B]. Its Laplace transform F must have subexponential decay of the displayed |s|^(3/4) form, up to growth in |Re s|, and satisfy Re F(s)>=0 for |Re s|<1. Scaling f by lambda gives phi_lambda(s)=lambda F(lambda(s-1)) and phi_lambda(s)=phi_lambda(2-s).

parents.title: Infinite convolution gives compact support and subexponential transform decay

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Smoothness and decay are traded quantitatively: the chosen scale sequence controls derivative growth, and optimizing the number of integrations by parts converts that growth profile into the transform exponent.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Infinite convolution bridges local tent kernels to a compactly supported smooth positive object; Fourier/Laplace transformation and optimized derivative estimates bridge regularity to spectral decay.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: The span constructs psi as an infinite convolution of scaled tents, obtains compact support, smoothness, evenness, nonnegativity and positive Fourier transform, proves derivative bounds, and optimizes repeated integration by parts for transform decay. The candidate correctly states that multiplication by the hyperbolic-secant-type factor produces f with the required spatial properties and stronger decay, while positivity is deferred.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: Scaled tents g_n use a_n=n(log+ n)^omega with 1<omega<=2, and their convolutions converge uniformly to an even, nonnegative C-infinity function psi supported in [-B,B], where B is the convergent sum of a_n^(-1). The Fourier transform remains positive and psi is normalized at zero. Differentiating the convolution gives |psi^(k)| bounded by a factorial times (log k)^(k omega); repeated integration by parts and an optimized k yield subexponential decay for its Laplace transform. Multiplying by a normalized hyperbolic-secant-type factor h preserves the spatial properties and strengthens the required decay for f=psi h.
